title: Why You Should Never Fear Misbehavior
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that fearing misbehavior is itself counterproductive, since a teacher who mentally absorbs even a small piece of what should be a student's own burden unconsciously behaves in ways -- nervous pacing, visible disappointment, added lectures, inconsistency, dulled personality -- that actually cause more misbehavior. He contends most teachers don't realize they're doing this, insisting it's an unavoidable phenomenon rather than a character flaw, and that the fix is to fully delegate the emotional and disciplinary burden to a thoroughly taught classroom management plan. Once students understand the teacher is not personally the source of consequences, but simply the plan's calm enforcer, he argues accountability lands fully and durably on students themselves, freeing the teacher to stop caring, emotionally, whether misbehavior happens at all.
points: Fearing misbehavior causes unconscious teacher behaviors -- nervous pacing, visible disappointment, added lectures, inconsistency -- that themselves increase misbehavior.
Most teachers are unaware they display these fear-driven behaviors, and the pattern is described as essentially universal and unavoidable if fear is present.
Fully delegating disciplinary and emotional burden to a thoroughly taught classroom management plan is presented as the solution to fear of misbehavior.
Once students see the teacher is not personally the source of consequences, accountability lands durably on students, effectively removing the teacher's need to fear misbehavior.
quotes: If you stress over the possibility of misbehavior, then it’s a sign your classroom management is in need of an overhaul.
They don’t realize that when they fear misbehavior, they naturally and subconsciously behave in ways that cause more misbehavior.
The solution is to let your classroom management plan do the dirty work for you. Lean on it entirely to manage behavior.

When students realize through your fair and detailed explanation and calm follow through that you are not your classroom management plan, and that the plan is for them and their protection and freedom to learn and enjoy school, everything changes.
It’s why emotionally you shouldn’t care a fig whether your students misbehave.
